headline: Passed ordinances on City Clerk duties and repealing Chapter 164; approved $15,000 for Coggshall Park playground and $20,000 STEAM grant.
summary: Councilors sent a $2,979,000 dam removal grant, $205,817.80 in budget deficit funding, and an $11,400,000 water borrowing order to the Finance Committee. They granted two Unitil utility pole petitions and a special legislation petition on Marisa R. Fleming's creditable service. A motion to suspend rules for a resolution honoring Ronald B. Ingemie failed 5-6, so the resolution went to the Legislative Affairs Committee.
decisions: Accepted the Appointments Committee report on new and re-appointments, 11-0.
Adopted the minutes of the October 6, 2026 council meeting, 11-0.
Approved expenditure of an approximate $20,000 United Way grant for weekly STEAM activities, 11-0.
Approved expenditure of a $15,000 Friends of Coggshall Park donation for a new playground, 11-0.
Approved $15,000 from the Henry F. Coggshall Trust for a new Coggshall Park playground, 11-0.
Granted special legislation petition on creditable service for Marisa R. Fleming, 10-0, with Fleming recused.
Granted Unitil's petition to relocate Pole #8 at 7 Beekman St., 11-0.
Granted Unitil's petition for a new midspan Pole #30A at 470 Alpine Road, 11-0.
Referred $2,979,000 grant for McTaggart Pond Dam removal to Finance Committee.
Referred $133,700 feasibility study for Overlook Reservoir Dam and Dike to Finance Committee.
Referred $150,000 for design and permitting of Ashby West Road culverts to Finance Committee.
Referred $22,658.40 for road repaving to Finance Committee.
Referred $260,000 grant for Riverfront Park Stage to Finance Committee.
Referred $40,000 for sidewalks to Memorial Middle School to Finance Committee.
Referred $64,575 for DEP clean-up costs at city-owned sites to Finance Committee.

Motion to suspend rules for the Ingemie resolution failed, 5-6.
Referred resolution honoring Ronald B. Ingemie to Legislative Affairs Committee.
Passed ordinance amending City Code §3-19 and §3-43 on City Clerk duties to final reading, 11-0.
Passed ordinance repealing General Ordinance Chapter 164 in its entirety to final reading, 11-0.

City of Fitchburg  
                             Massachusetts 01420  
 
                     CITY COUNCIL  
            
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
The regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Fitchburg was held at the Legislative Building 
at 700 Main Street and over the Zoom meeting platform and live streamed at FATV Studios, 
Fitchburg, on October 20, 2026.   
 
The meeting was called to orde r by President Zarrella at 7:12 P.M.  The meeting opened with a 
salute to the Flag led by  Council or Fleming. The City Clerk c alled the roll 11 Councilors were 
present, (Councilor Cruz via zoom). Board consists of 11 members.  
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
I. PUBLIC FORUM 
  
No one spoke during Public Forum. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
II. ANNOUNCEMENTS 
 
The next meeting of the Widowed Helping Widowed Support Group will take place on Thursday, 
October 29 from 4 until 5:30 p.m. in Room 205 at the Fitchburg State University Recreation 
Center, 130 North Street.  Kelley Lynn, Kathy Boisvert, and Bernie Schultz will co-facilitate the 
meeting. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
The City of Fitchburg Health Department invites the community to meet substance use disorder 
treatment providers and explore the range of treatment options available on Wednesday, October 
21 from 5pm-7pm at the Fitchburg Armory. Representatives from detox facilities, medication-
assisted therapy, peer recovery centers, sober homes, family support services and more.  
This is a free public event and refreshments will be served.  
 
The City of Fitchburg Health Department will again partner with the Fitchburg Police Department 
to participate in National Prescription Drug Take Back Day on Saturday, October 24, 2026 from 
9am-11am at the Municipal Parking Garage, Upper level, 412 Main Street.  
This initiative offers a safe, convenient and responsible way to dispose of unused or expired 
prescription drugs and get them out of circulation. Residents may "drive up and drop off" without 
leaving your vehicle. All materials are collected anonymously and will be taken directly by the 
Police Department to a regional drop off site to be incinerated.  
 
Please contact Sue Christensen at (978) 829-1854 for more information on either program.  
Councilors at Large 
    Sally H. Cragin 
Amy L. Green 
Kevin T. Starr  
Elizabeth R. Walsh 
Anthony M. Zarrella 
 
President 
Anthony M. Zarrella 
 
Vice President 
Derrick J. Cruz 
         Ward Councilors 
   Ward 1 – Bernard J. Schultz III 
   Ward 2 – Paul R. Beauchemin 
   Ward 3 – Joseph S. Bowen, Jr. 
   Ward 4 – Andrew J. Van Hazinga 
   Ward 5 – Marisa R. Fleming 
   Ward 6 – Derrick J. Cruz
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
Thursday, October 29, at 6:00 p.m. Bill Chittick will present a talk entitled: “What is so rare as a 
day in June?” It's about Worcester’s Tornado of 1953. Bill Chittick will share the astonishing story 
of how all eyes were turned to Worcester, Massachusetts in 1953 after it was ravaged by a tornado. 
This talk is free and will take place at the Fitchburg Historical Society, 781 Main Street. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
On Thursday, November 5,  from 4:30 to 6:00 p.m. The Fitchburg Historical Society and Fitchburg 
Access TV invite people to come and talk about  Local History and Memory and then possibly 
Share Their Story by using FATV's podcast studio.  
 
There will also be a brief talk by Susan Navarre on recent Fitchburg history to get ideas flowing! 
Join us at Fitchburg Access TV, 780 Main St., on November 5 to Share your stories. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
All invited to Ansin Park, Clean-up Day and Open House on Sunday, October 25, from 10 am to 4 
pm at 40 Appleton Circle Fitchburg.  
 
Whether you can spare an hour or more, we'd appreciate the help clearing leaves, working inside 
the concession stand and other projects around the park. You can also see the park in action as 
some of our youngest players, T-Ball kids, take the field.  
 
Donuts will be served in the morning and pizza at 12:30 pm. Contact Jason Morse 
at ozmyn@hotmail.com or visit "Ansin Park" on Facebook 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
November 3, 2026 State Election – Important Voter Information 
 
Reminder for voters of several important dates and deadlines for the upcoming State Election on 
Tuesday, November 3, 2026. 
 
In-person early voting is currently underway at Fitchburg City Hall and will continue through 
Friday, October 30. 
 
The remaining early voting hours are as follows: 
• Monday, October 19 through Friday, October 23: 8:30 AM – 4:30 PM 
• Saturday, October 24: 10:00 AM – 2:00 PM 
• Sunday, October 25: 9:00 AM – 1:00 PM 
• Monday, October 26 through Friday, October 30: 8:30 AM – 4:30 PM 
I would also like to remind residents of two important deadlines: 
• Saturday, October 24 is the last day to register to vote for this upcoming State Election. 
The City Clerk's Office will be open from 9:00 AM to 5:00 PM for voter registration. 
• Tuesday, October 27 at 5:00 PM is the deadline for the City Clerk's Office to receive 
applications for Vote by Mail ballots.
Voters have three options for casting their ballots: 
1. Vote by Mail. 
2. Vote early in person at Fitchburg City Hall through October 30. 
3. Vote in person on Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, at their assigned polling location. 
Polls will be open from 7:00 AM to 8:00 PM. 
Residents can check their voter registration status, track their Vote by Mail ballot, and find their 
assigned polling location through the Massachusetts Secretary of the Commonwealth's website at 
www.VoteInMA.com. 
   
Anyone with questions or needing assistance is encouraged to contact the Fitchburg City Clerk's 
Office at 978-829-1820. 
 
Thank you, and I encourage all eligible Fitchburg residents to make a plan to vote in the November 
3 State Election.

162-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg hereby approves the expenditure of grant

 (Be Adopted)

 Special Legislation Relative to Creditable Service

VI. PUBLIC HEARINGS 
 
Motion and second to take Public Hearing out of order. 
 
169-26. 7 BEEKMAN ST – Unitil petitions to relocate Pole #8 (Salem St.). The proposed 
Pole #8 would be relocated approximately 26 feet from its original location and 
would be situated approximately 80 feet from Beekman St. and approximately 415 
feet from Spruce St., Fitchburg. 
 
President Zarrella declared the Public Hearing open at 7:24 PM 
 
Mr. John Kimball, from Unitil, spoke and explained that the reason for the pole relocation is that 
the customer plans to install a driveway in that exact location. Therefore, the utility pole must be 
relocated to accommodate the driveway and allow construction of the proposed multi-unit 
development. 
 
No one spoke in favor to the petition. 
 
No one spoke in opposition to the petition. 
 
President Zarrella declared the hearing closed at 7:24 PM 
 
Motion and second to grant petition by roll call vote 11 in favor and 0 opposed. 11 members  
Present. Board consists of 11 members. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
170-26. 470 ALPINE ROAD – Unitil petitions to install a new midspan Pole #30A on 
Alpine Road. The proposed Pole #30A would be situated approximately 52 feet 
from existing Pole #30 and approximately 997 feet from the intersection of 
McIntire Road, Fitchburg. 
 
President Zarrella declared the Public Hearing open at 7:26 PM 
 
Mr. John Kimball, from Unitil, spoke and explained that the proposed pole installation is related to 
the solar farm project on Alpine Road. The pole is needed to serve as the solar farm’s takeoff pole, 
with the location determined by property line constraints. He further clarified that the project must 
be processed under Section 30A rather than Section 30. 
 
No one spoke in favor to the petition. 
 
No one spoke in opposition to the petition. 
 
President Zarrella declared the hearing closed at 7:26 PM 
 
Motion and second to grant petition by roll call vote 11 in favor and 0 opposed. 11 members  
Present. Board consists of 11 members. 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
VII. ORDERS – FINANCE 
    
Waive reading, Orders stand referred to Finance Committee: 
 
172-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg appropriate grant funds in the approximate 
amount of TWO MILLION NINE HUNDRED SEVENTY-NINE THOUSAND 
DOLLARS ($2,979,000) from the Executive Office of Energy and Environmental 
Affairs Eco One Stop Grant to complete the construction phase of the McTaggart 
Pond Dam Removal and Phillips Brook Restoration Project.   
 
173-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg appropriate grant funds in the approximate 
amount of ONE HUNDRED THIRTY-THREE THOUSAND SEVEN HUNDRED 
DOLLARS ($133,700) from the Executive Office of Energy and Environmental 
Affairs Eco One Stop Grant to conduct a feasibility study to assess removal of the 
Overlook Reservoir Dam and Dike, or lowering the normal pool elevations. 
 
174-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg appropriate grant funds in the approximate 
amount of ONE HUNDRED FIFTY THOUSAND DOLLARS ($150,000) to 
advance the design and permitting for two replacement culverts along Ashby West 
Road. 
 
175-26. ORDER THAT: there be and hereby is appropriated the sum of TWENTY-TWO 
THOUSAND SIX HUNDRED FIFTY-EIGHT AND 40/100 DOLLARS 
($22,658.40) same to be charged against RESERVED FOR APPROPRIATION - 
TNC PER RIDE ASSESSMENT and credited to DPW CAPITAL EXPENSES - 
STREET REPAIR for the purpose of road repaving. 
 
176-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg appropriate grant funds in the approximate 
amount of TWO HUNDRED SIXTY THOUSAND DOLLARS ($260,000) from 
the U.S. Department of the Interior, through the Massachusetts Executive Office of 
Energy and Environmental Affairs Land and Water Conservation Grant Fund, 
toward construction of the Riverfront Park Stage. 
The total project cost is $520,000; this reimbursable grant will supplement previous 
appropriations from New Vue Communities, State Earmarks, Beers for Good, and 
CDBG Year 52. 
 
177-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg appropriate FORTY THOUSAND 
DOLLARS ($40,000) from RESERVE FOR MUNICIPAL PURPOSES for title 
searches, appraisals, and easements related to the construction of new sidewalks 
leading to Memorial Middle School. 
 
178-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg appropriate SIXTY-FOUR THOUSAND 
FIVE HUNDRED SEVENTY-FIVE DOLLARS ($64,575) from RESERVE FOR 
MUNICIPAL PURPOSES to address DEP clean-up costs at several city-owned 
sites.
179-26. ORDER THAT: the City of Fitchburg appropriate TWO HUNDRED FIVE 
THOUSAND EIGHT HUNDRED SEVENTEEN AND 80/100 DOLLARS 
($205,817.80) from RESERVE FOR MUNICIPAL PURPOSES to cover the 
following Fiscal Year 2026 budget deficits: 
 
LAW OTHER EXPENSES – Labor Negotiator  $197.39 
BOARD OF HEALTH – Rubbish Removal   $4,420.26 
BOARD OF HEALTH – Sanitary Landfill Expenses $61,110.18 
EMPLOYEE BENEFITS – Workers Compensation  $139,810.35 
EMPLOYEE BENEFITS – Medicare   $279.62 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
VIII. LOAN ORDER 
 
Waive reading, Loan Order stands referred to Finance Committee: 
 
180-26. LOAN ORDER: that Loan Order #019-25, which was ordered by this Council on 
March 18, 2025 and authorized a borrowing of $11,400,000 for various water 
projects, is hereby amended by replacing it in its entirety to read as follows:  
 
  ORDERED:  That $11,400,000 aggregate amount is appropriated for the following 
  projects, including all costs incidental and related thereto, which amount may be  
  apportioned to such projects as needed to accomplish the projects: (i) rehabilitation 
  and/or upgrade of the Meetinghouse Gatehouse and Mare Meadow/Bickford Pump                
                        Station, at an estimated cost of $4,220,000; (ii) Main Street water main replacement  
   project, at an estimated cost of $3,290,000, which amount is expected to be used in  
addition to certain American Rescue Plan Act funds available for the project; (iii)  
Regional Water Treatment Plant roof replacement and/or weatherproofing project,  
at an estimated cost of $740,000; (iv) Water Street water main replacement project,  
at an estimated cost of $1,750,000; and (v) Exeter Street and Rodimon Avenue  
water main replacement projects, including fire hydrants and domestic/fire service  
lines, at an estimated cost of $1,400,000, which amount is expected to be used in  
addition certain other funds available through the City’s annual operating budget;  
and that to meet this appropriation the Treasurer with the approval of the Mayor is  
authorized to borrow $11,400,000 under G.L. c.44, §8 or any other enabling  
authority; that the Mayor is authorized to contract for and expend any federal or  
state aid available for the projects; that the Mayor is authorized to take any other  
action necessary to carry out the projects; and that the Treasurer is authorized to file  
an application with the Municipal Finance Oversight Board to qualify under  
Chapter 44A of the General Laws any or all of the bonds authorized by this order  
and to provide such information and execute such documents as the Municipal  
Finance Oversight Board may require for these purposes. 
(Refer to Finance) 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
IX. RESOLUTION 
 
Motion and second for suspension of rules by roll call vote 5 in favor and 6 opposed (Councilor  
Bowen, Cragin, Green, Van Hazinga, Walsh and President Zarrella). The motion for Suspension of  
rules failed. Resolution stands referred to the Legislative Affairs Committee. 11 members present.  
Board consists of 11 members. 
 
181-26. RESOLUTION: NOW BE IT THEREFORE RESOLVED that the City Council of 
Fitchburg thanks and honors Ronald B. Ingemie for his distinguished service and 
lasting contributions to the City and its residents; and 
 
BE IT FURTHER RESOLVED that a portrait of Ron Ingemie and a plaque 
memorializing his service, the same to be donated by private parties, be displayed in 
the Legislative Building. 
(Legislative Affairs) 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
X. ORDINANCES 
 
166-26. AN ORDINANCE: President Zarrella and Vice President Cruz, to amend §3-19 and 
§3-43 of the City Code, concerning the management and responsibilities of the City 
Clerk, as detailed in the enclosed ordinance. 
 Amend §3-19 and §3-43 of the City Code 
 (Final Reading) 
 
Motion and second to pass Ordinance to a third and final reading, and adopt to be enrolled and 
ordained by roll call vote 11 in favor and 0 opposed. 11 members present. Board consists of 11 
members.  
 
Ordinance signed by the Mayor October , 2026. 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
167-26.         AN ORDINANCE: That the General Ordinance of the City of Fitchburg, Chapter 164, 
shall be repealed in its entirety. 
 Ref. petition 150-26 
 (Final Reading) 
 
Motion and second to pass Ordinance to a third and final reading, and adopt to be enrolled and 
ordained by roll call vote 11 in favor and 0 opposed. 11 members present. Board consists of 11 
members.  
 
Ordinance signed by the Mayor October , 2026. 
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
XI. PETITIONS 
 
The following petitions stand referred to the Public Safety Committee: 
 
182-26. Councilor Fleming, on behalf of Darren Plante, requests the installation of a 
guardrail or other suitable barrier in front of the fence at Fitchburg Storage, located 
at 149 Upham Street. This measure is intended to prevent further damage to the 
fence caused by vehicles traveling at excessive speeds from JFH, rounding the 
corner toward Jackson Avenue. 
 (Public Safety) 
 
183-26. Councilor Fleming, on behalf of Samuel Blair of 304 High Rock Rd. requests the 
installation of a stop sign or flashing slow-down sign on Richardson Rd heading 
towards Ashby State Rd. at the High Rock Rd intersection. Increased traffic has 
made it dangerous to exit High Rock Rd due to low visibility and speeding vehicles. 
  (Public Safety) 
----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- 
 
 
 
 
XI. OTHER BUSINESS 
 
Special Meeting of the Fitchburg City Council – Tax Classification 
Wednesday, October 28, 2026  
 Immediately following the Finance Committee meeting, which begins at 6:00 PM 
 
Next Regular City Council Meeting 
Wednesday, November 4, 2026 7:00 PM 
 
 
The meeting adjourned at 7:35 P.M. 
 
 
___________________________________       
Joanna Bilotta-Simeone, City Clerk
